text:
maria: Heads up — we saw a spike of streaming failures during a spot reclaim in eu-west-1 around 08:11 UTC. Root cause looks like partial token cutover + aggressive drain window. 5xxs for ~90s, client reconnects failed to resume in many cases.

leo: ugh. any logs? was the requeue header set?

maria: logs show client side saw EOF and then a 502 on the resume POST. server log snippet: `stream.disconnect: reason=eviction, lease=preemptible, drain_deadline=20s, resume_token_missing=true`

jin: Were we doing token streaming cutover (stream proxy hands off a resume token) or full reconnect? two different code paths.

maria: streaming-proxy attempted to hand off. It returned a `X-Resume-Token` but our ingress dropped it during failure, looks like race between drain completion and node termination.

andrew: can we increase the drain window on preemptible nodes when there are active streams? tradeoff vs capacity/cost though.

tara: +1, but increasing drain window by default hurts utilization. Suggest a conditional: 1) short grace for bursty inference (<10s), 2) extended grace if in-progress streaming requests with resume tokens and client version >=1.4.0.

leo: also consider QoS routing: if a pool is saturated and eviction is imminent, prefer routing short non-streaming requests to that pool and keep longer streams on on-demand/dedicated. 

maria: that matches my thinking. We could mark instances with `eviction_risk=high` in the routing layer and bias by `request.qos=best_effort|streaming|interactive`.

jin: implementation notes: we need three pieces: `1) drain handshake extension` (only when token available), `2) reliable resume header propagation` (preserve across proxies), `3) requeue fallback window` (client-visible ttl for resume).

andrew: for (2) might be easiest to add an explicit signed resume blob attached to the request body, not just a header — persists in our requeue queue if ingress drops headers. example proto: ```{"resume_token":"abc..","expiry":1650000000,"sig":"..."}```

maria: good. fallback policy: if resume fails within 60s, autoplace into requeue queue with `attempts=3` and route to on-demand fallback pool. 

tara: how do we keep costs in check? too many fallbacks -> on-demand burn. maybe use budget throttle: allow fallback up to X qps per region per hour, then start draining streams earlier?

leo: we should add observability dims: `resume_success_rate`, `requeue_rate`, `fallback_on_demand_rate`, and a cost counter `tokens_fallback_usd`. Hook alerts if resume_success_rate < 95% for 5m.

maria: agreed. I'll sketch a proposal: *conditional drain policy* + *signed resume blob persisted on requeue* + *QoS routing labels* + *fallback budget with alerting*. I'll put a design doc.

jin: small nit: signed blob increases storage/IO on requeue queue. for high-qps streaming we must TTL aggressively and compact.

andrew: also update client SDK: expose `resume_ttl` and auto-retry behavior. Opt-in for older clients.

ops-bot: deploy plan checklist created: https://go/repo/evict-resume-design draft -> please review by EOD Thu :clipboard:

maria: thanks all — can someone own the QoS routing stub? @leo?

leo: I can take QoS routing and metrics. will add a short RFC.

tara: I'll own cost guardrails and fallback budget config.

jin: I'll do the resume blob + requeue queue changes.

andrew: I'll update client SDK plan.

sre-bot: noted: creating incident retro ticket to store postmortem notes and attach timeline.

maria: great. we'll aim for a canary in eu-west-1 nightly and validate resume_success_rate and cost delta. :thumbsup:
